papers.title: Effect of Multi-Modal Training in Patients With Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial.
papers.reason: The trial measures global cognitive improvement in MCI but provides only exploratory attention results and no executive-function-specific modelling or biomarker analysis.

papers.title: Unraveling the roles of anemia, renal impairment, and neuroinflammation in hemodialysis-associated cognitive dysfunction in chronic kidney disease patients.
papers.reason: The title indicates a clinical investigation of general cognitive dysfunction and its medical correlates without an evident focus on executive processes or computational assessment.

papers.title: Feasibility of immersive 40 Hz gamma sensory stimulation in early-stage Alzheimer's disease.
papers.reason: The study combines EEG and memory performance in early Alzheimer's disease, but its principal focus is gamma-stimulation feasibility rather than executive function.

papers.title: Comparative efficacy of various non-pharmacological therapies on cognitive function in patients with mild cognitive impairment or dementia: A network meta-analysis.
papers.reason: The meta-analysis evaluates interventions using global cognitive scales without isolating executive-function mechanisms, task signatures, or biomarkers.

papers.title: Shared Variance Across Cognitive Assessments Predicts Language Outcomes in Aphasia: A Preliminary Study.
papers.reason: The paper concerns cognitive assessment in aphasia, but the available title does not establish a substantive focus on planning, working memory, attention, or cognitive control.

papers.title: A previously unreported ELOVL4 frameshift variant in a patient with early severe cognitive decline, parkinsonism, and cerebellar ataxia: A case report.
papers.reason: This single-patient genetic case documents severe global cognitive impairment but offers no executive-function-specific findings or quantitative cognitive model.

papers.title: Rationale, Design, and Baseline Characteristics of the TARGET (Targeted Assessment and Recruitment of Geriatrics for Effective Fall Prevention Treatments) Cohort of Older Adults for Assessing Fall and Fracture Risk: Prospective Cohort Study
papers.reason: The cohort integrates VR cognitive assessment, wearable gait data, clinical records, and predictive modelling, although its primary outcome is fall and fracture risk rather than cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Identifying Cognitive Impairment in People Who Are Homeless in Metropolitan Australia: An Exploratory Study.
papers.reason: The study uses interview indicators and regression to prioritize general cognitive assessment referrals but lacks executive-function tasks, physiological biomarkers, or digital measures.

papers.title: A shared EEG signal for the maintenance of visually and linguistically evoked objects: theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling.
papers.reason: Two EEG experiments identify theta-gamma coupling as a candidate neural mechanism for actively maintaining multiple representations in working memory.

papers.title: Effects and safety of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation on cognitive outcomes in mild cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.reason: The review links stimulation parameters to cognitive outcomes in MCI, but its pooled measures emphasize global cognition and memory rather than executive-function mechanisms.

papers.title: Sleep spindle deficits in childhood absence epilepsy improve with antiseizure treatment and disease resolution
papers.reason: The EEG findings establish frontal sleep-spindle rate as a physiological marker of epilepsy state and cognitive vulnerability, but they do not directly measure executive performance.
